text:
Reaction 1 is a classical acid-induced pinacol (semi-pinacol) rearrangement: a 1,2-diol is converted into a ketone by conc. H₂SO₄.  
Therefore A must be a vicinal diol, not a mono-alcohol.  
The only option that supplies a diol precursor is 2,7-dimethyloctahydronaphthalene-4a,8a-diol.

Reaction 2 is the base-promoted [2,3]-Wittig rearrangement of an allyl benzyl ether.  n-BuLi deprotonates the benzylic position; the resulting carbanion undergoes the [2,3] shift and protonation to give the homoallylic benzyl alcohol 4-methyl-1-phenylpent-3-en-1-ol.  
Hence B must be an allyl benzyl ether, i.e. (((3-methylbut-2-en-1-yl)oxy)methyl)benzene.

The only choice matching both requirements is:

C) A = 2,7-dimethyloctahydronaphthalene-4a,8a-diol,  
  B = (((3-methylbut-2-en-1-yl)oxy)methyl)benzene

Answer: C
